title: Iran War Volatility, Private Credit Fears Grow, & Solar Continues to Crash | The Weekly Wrap
summary: Eisman attributes market swings to changing war and credit narratives, flags retail and institutional redemption pressure, and remains cautious on solar and health insurance. The Elevance regulatory problem was real, but the threatened sanctions were conditional and later recorded as corrected. He explicitly leaves AI-driven mass unemployment and life-insurer credit losses unproven. His categorical no-credit-cycle-since-GFC statement is too broad; evidence of market anxiety is distinct from realized systemic loss.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
framework_points: Distinguish a narrative reversal from new realized losses.
Look for loan growth and weak diligence before credit trouble.
Follow financing costs and subsidies in solar.
Separate duration matching at insurers from asset credit and hidden leverage concerns.
tools_and_charts: Medicare Advantage sanctions and star ratings
transcript_cautions: The MongoDB guidance sentence lacks a verb in captions; context describes weak guidance.
MFS is identified as Market Financial Solutions in this episode.
Viewer criticism of asset-manager ownership is not an assertion by Eisman.
